function.name: calculate_time
function.description: Calculates the time taken to cover a distance at a certain speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance.description: The distance to be covered in meters. This is a float type value.

speed.description: The speed at which the object is moving in m/s. This is a float type value.

round_to_nearest_second.description: Optional parameter to round the time to the nearest second.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have direct access to a live clock, so I can’t give you the exact current time. If you let me know your timezone (or whether you’re looking for UTC), I could help explain how to find it on most devices.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What's the time right now?" We need current local time. According to system instructions we should not provide real-time data unless it's from an external source or built-in knowledge. But as per policy, providing accurate current time might violate privacy if location unknown. However this request seems straightforward; but we don't have actual clock access. In such cases, best practice is to say cannot determine exact time due to lack of context and no ability to fetch real-time info.

We can respond with something like: I can't tell you the precise current time because I'm not connected to a live clock. If they want approximate, maybe mention UTC offset etc. So answer accordingly.
